name: Single-line editable layout row splice

atomicDiscipline.rule: Run exactly the printed hypothesis. If the attempted change fails, degrades, or suggests a different fix, revert to the checkpoint and finish this experiment as failure. Start a new experiment for the next idea.

primaryTarget: headed WASM WebGPU TextArea edit fixture
hypothesisMarkdown:
# Hypothesis

For an identity-projection edit that replaces bytes within one logical row without changing that
row's byte length or introducing a newline, the layout map can retain every unaffected `LayoutRow`
and only reshape/splice the changed row. Any style, projection, line-count, or geometry condition
outside that narrow invariant falls back to the existing full update.

## Scope lock

This experiment only carries a precise `TextEdit` from editable state to layout and splices the
single safe row. It does not generalize insertion/deletion, multi-line changes, projections, or
font/style invalidation.
measurementPlanMarkdown:
# Measurement plan

Add a deterministic differential test that applies a same-length single-line edit to a 2,000-line
buffer and compares offset/position/visual-row parity with the full update. Run the focused headed
WASM/WebGPU TextArea editing fixture at both DPRs and inspect its screenshot; retain raw timing and
work-counter artifacts.
expectedOutcomeMarkdown:
# Expected outcome

The safe edit shapes exactly one row and retains stable metadata/layout allocations for every
other row. Unsafe edits use the existing complete update, preserving projection, styles, UTF-8,
wrapping, caret, selection, and scroll behavior.
reportMarkdown:
## Single-line editable layout row splice

The same-length, single-logical-line edit path reshapes and replaces only the changed row when the installed layout is unprojected, unstyled, and geometry-preserving. Every other edit takes the existing full layout path.

### Focused WASM validation

- `cargo run -p xtask -- check-source-guard` passed.
- `cargo run -p xtask -- app apps/test_suite test wasm --headed --webgpu --playwright-test test_suite/rayx-text-area-edit-performance.spec.ts` passed at DPR 1 and DPR 2.
- The dedicated Test Suite page is `/performance/text-area-edit`; its action selects and replaces one visible character in a 2,000-line `TextArea`.
- The DPR 2 screenshot shows the edited character and retained caret with no text or scroll corruption.

### Measurement protocol

The headed Chromium WebGPU run used one worker, both configured DPR projects, 35 repeats per project, and discarded the first five samples per project. It produced 30 measured samples at each DPR and no failures.

| DPR | p50 input-to-published-frame | p95 | changed pixels |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 185.2906 ms | 207.9167 ms | 2,857 |
| 2 | 176.5264 ms | 203.7505 ms | 10,784 |

Raw Playwright artifacts remain in `11-single-line-layout-row-splice-output/`; they are intentionally untracked.

### Decision

Accept. The targeted path keeps UTF-8 row boundaries, existing visual-row metadata, and unchanged shaped layouts intact while strictly falling back for newlines, style runs, projections, length changes, duplicate old rows, and a possible maximum-width reduction. The focused source test checks that a 2,000-row same-length edit reports one shaped row and 1,999 reused rows while matching full-layout coordinate geometry.
decisionMarkdown:
## Decision

Accept the safe same-length single-line splice. It preserves the installed unprojected layout and shapes only the edited row; all edits outside those explicit invariants continue through the complete layout update.
